findings.title: Missing double-check of cache after acquiring write lock
findings.body: After the first (read-locked) check of entryPointAssetsCache fails (e.g., cache not yet populated or cfg.Env == Dev), the code acquires the write lock at line 48 but never re-checks whether another goroutine already populated the cache while waiting for the lock. As a result, under concurrent initial requests (common right after startup), multiple goroutines can all proceed past the first check, serialize on the write lock, and each redundantly re-read and re-parse assets-manifest.json (or hit the CDN) even though the first goroutine already finished and stored a valid result. This doesn't reintroduce the data race, but it defeats part of the purpose of caching and wastes I/O/CPU under load. A standard fix is to re-check `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` immediately after acquiring the write lock and return early if so.

findings.title: No regression test added for the data race fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the global entryPointAssetsCache variable in GetWebAssets, but no test was added (e.g., a test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently from multiple goroutines, intended to be run with `go test -race`) to guard against regressions. Without such a test, a future refactor could silently reintroduce the race with no automated signal.
